workflow_summary: The developer wants an agent that automatically sends order-status updates (e.g., order confirmed, shipped, delayed, delivered) to their customers. Since the specific channel(s) and backend were not specified by the user, this research assumes a typical setup: order data originates from an e-commerce/order-management backend (Shopify or WooCommerce as representative examples), and updates are pushed to customers via email and/or SMS, with WhatsApp as an optional richer channel — plus a mechanism to confirm messages were actually delivered and to respect opt-outs/bounces.

tasks.task_description: Retrieve order status/shipment data from an e-commerce or order-management backend to know what update to send.

recommended_apis.rationale: Shopify is one of the most widely used hosted e-commerce platforms; its Admin API exposes order, fulfillment, and customer data needed to compose an update, and supports webhooks (order/updated, fulfillments/create, etc.) for event-driven triggering instead of polling.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: GET /admin/api/latest/orders.json (list orders, status=any), GET /admin/api/latest/orders/{order_id}.json (single order incl. fulfillment_status, financial_status), POST for order webhooks subscription (via GraphQL webhookSubscriptionCreate). Order cancel/close/open endpoints exist but are destructive and should not be exposed to a notification agent.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: REST Admin API is legacy (frozen Oct 2024); new integrations should target GraphQL Admin API. Requires OAuth app approval/install and access-token scopes (read_orders); only last 60 days of orders visible without a granted read_all_orders scope; reading customer billing/shipping PII requires separate 'protected customer data' approval from Shopify — a real approval/review hurdle for an agent that needs customer contact details.
open_questions: Which e-commerce platform does the developer actually use (Shopify, WooCommerce, custom, other)?
Will the agent use REST or is it required to migrate to GraphQL Admin API for new integrations?
Does the developer need historical (>60 day) order access, requiring extra scope approval?

recommended_apis.rationale: For self-hosted WordPress/WooCommerce stores, this is the direct equivalent of Shopify's Admin API — exposes orders with status field (pending/processing/completed/etc.) needed to determine what update to send, with no third-party app-review process since the merchant controls their own keys.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: GET /wp-json/wc/v3/orders (list, filterable by status), GET /wp-json/wc/v3/orders/{id} (single order with status, line_items, billing/shipping). No official push webhooks are documented on this page (WooCommerce does support webhooks separately via wp-admin UI) so polling or store-side webhook configuration is needed.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Self-hosted means reliability/uptime is the merchant's responsibility; requires Basic Auth consumer key/secret which must be transmitted over HTTPS (or exposed in query string as fallback, less secure); versioning/plugin updates can break custom integrations; no automatic delivery-status linkage to notifications (must be built by the MCP layer).
open_questions: Does the store have WooCommerce webhooks configured/enabled, or will the agent need to poll periodically?

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: Expose a read-only 'get_order_status' / 'list_recent_orders' tool per backend (Shopify, WooCommerce) that returns normalized order fields (order id, customer contact info, status, tracking info, last-updated timestamp). Do NOT expose order create/update/cancel/delete endpoints through this MCP server — the agent's job is notification, not order management, so mutating endpoints are out of scope and a security/destructive-action risk. Prefer wiring backend webhooks (Shopify order/fulfillment webhooks) to push events into the agent's queue rather than having the MCP tool poll, to reduce latency and API usage.

tasks.task_description: Send transactional order-update notifications via email.

recommended_apis.rationale: Mature, well-documented transactional email API with dynamic templating (ideal for standardized 'order shipped'/'order delivered' templates), scheduling, and categorization — widely used for exactly this order-update use case.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST /v3/mail/send (single/templated send with personalizations, dynamic_template_data, send_at scheduling); Event Webhook for delivery/bounce/open/click/unsubscribe tracking.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Requires sender identity/domain verification before sending; free tier has volume caps and stricter deliverability scrutiny; EU data-residency sending requires a paid Pro-plan subuser; must implement webhook signature verification for trustworthy delivery tracking.
open_questions: What email sending volume is expected (affects plan/tier choice)?

recommended_apis.rationale: Positioned specifically for transactional (not marketing) email with strong deliverability reputation management and separate 'MessageStream' concept that keeps transactional order emails isolated from bulk/marketing traffic — a good fit if the developer wants a lean, focused vendor.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST /email (single send with templates via TemplateAlias/TemplateModel), POST /email/batch (bulk send of individual personalized order updates).
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Smaller ecosystem/fewer regions than SendGrid; still requires sender signature/domain verification; pricing is per-email and can be less flexible at very high volume compared to SendGrid's tiers (not independently verified — should be confirmed on pricing page before commit).
open_questions: Has the developer verified Postmark's current pricing tiers against expected email volume?

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: Expose a single 'send_order_email' tool that accepts recipient, template name/id, and structured order-data variables, internally mapping to the provider's template-send call (SendGrid dynamic_template_data or Postmark TemplateModel). Do not expose raw arbitrary HTML/content sending or bulk marketing-list features — keep the tool narrowly scoped to templated transactional sends to avoid spam/abuse risk and preserve sender reputation. A separate 'get_email_status' tool backed by the provider's event webhook store can let the agent check delivery/bounce state before retrying via an alternate channel.

recommended_apis.rationale: Industry-standard SMS API, simple send call, strong global coverage, and status-callback webhooks for delivery tracking — a natural fit for short order-status texts.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST /2010-04-01/Accounts/{AccountSid}/Messages.json (create message: body, from, to, optional StatusCallback URL).
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Requires purchasing/provisioning a phone number (or Messaging Service with number pool) and passing carrier registration (e.g., A2P 10DLC in the US) for application-to-person traffic — a real compliance/approval hurdle before production sending; trial accounts can only message verified numbers.
open_questions: Does the target customer base require A2P 10DLC or other local carrier registration (varies by country)?

recommended_apis.rationale: Comparable global SMS provider with a unified Messages API that can also address WhatsApp/Messenger/Viber through the same request shape (channel field), useful if the developer later wants to consolidate multi-channel sending under one vendor.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST https://rest.nexmo.com/sms/:format (legacy SMS API) or POST to Messages API with channel:'sms', webhook_url for delivery callback.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Two parallel APIs (legacy SMS API vs newer Messages API) can create confusion about which to use; same regulatory/number-provisioning burdens as Twilio for production A2P messaging; documentation is comparatively less detailed on this crawl than Twilio's.
open_questions: Which Vonage API (legacy SMS vs Messages API) best fits long-term multi-channel plans?

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: Expose a 'send_order_sms' tool taking recipient phone number (E.164) and a short pre-approved message/template, with StatusCallback wired to a 'get_sms_status' tool. Do not expose two-way conversational SMS handling or number-provisioning/account-management endpoints — those are operational/admin concerns outside the notification agent's scope.

tasks.task_description: Send order-update notifications via WhatsApp/rich messaging (optional additional channel).

recommended_apis.rationale: Direct, official API from Meta for WhatsApp messaging, supports rich message types (images, buttons, lists) well suited to order tracking/visual updates, and is free of a third-party BSP fee if self-managed.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: POST /<PHONE_NUMBER_ID>/messages for service (freeform) messages within a 24h customer-service window; template messages (Utility templates) required for proactive out-of-window order updates.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Requires Meta Business verification, phone number registration, and pre-approval of message templates used for proactive/out-of-session notifications (the common case for order updates) — an approval process that can take time and be rejected; customers must have opted in to WhatsApp messaging.
open_questions: Has the business completed Meta Business verification and WhatsApp number registration?
Are order-update templates already drafted and approved, or does that approval need to be budgeted into the project timeline?

recommended_apis.rationale: Lets a team reuse the same Twilio account/credentials and SDK used for SMS to also send WhatsApp messages (just prefixing numbers with 'whatsapp:'), simplifying a multi-channel MCP tool design at the cost of an added BSP layer.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: client.messages.create with from/to prefixed 'whatsapp:+E164'; Content API (contentSid + contentVariables) for sending pre-approved templates outside the 24h session.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Still subject to the exact same Meta template-approval and 24-hour session rules as the native Cloud API, plus Twilio's own per-message fees on top of Meta's; onboarding requires WhatsApp Sender registration through Twilio console.
open_questions: Is the added cost/complexity of a BSP (Twilio) justified versus using Meta's Cloud API directly, given the team already needs Twilio for SMS?

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: If WhatsApp is required, expose a 'send_order_whatsapp_template' tool restricted to pre-approved template sends (never freeform arbitrary text) so the MCP server can't accidentally violate the 24-hour session rule or WhatsApp's policy on unsolicited messaging. Treat this as an optional channel added only after the developer confirms Meta Business verification and template approval are in place.

tasks.task_description: Track delivery status, handle bounces/opt-outs/failures across channels.

recommended_apis.rationale: Native, well-documented mechanism to receive per-message delivery status (queued/sent/delivered/failed/undelivered/read) for both SMS and Twilio-routed WhatsApp messages, enabling retry logic or fallback to another channel.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: StatusCallback webhook (configured per-message or per-Messaging Service) POSTs MessageStatus + ErrorCode to the developer's endpoint.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: High-volume senders can receive a 'callback storm' (multiple POSTs per message); webhook endpoint must be publicly reachable and should validate Twilio's request signature to avoid spoofed status updates.

recommended_apis.rationale: Equivalent mechanism for the email channel: delivers delivered/bounce/blocked/spamreport/unsubscribe events so the agent can mark an email as failed, suppress future sends to bounced/opted-out addresses, or trigger a fallback SMS.
recommended_apis.important_endpoints: Event Webhook POST of a JSON array of event objects (email, event, timestamp, sg_message_id, reason) to a configured URL; ECDSA signature verification available.
recommended_apis.potential_challenges: Must build persistent storage/suppression list logic yourself (SendGrid also maintains its own internal suppression lists for bounces/spam reports, which can silently block later sends unless separately managed via SendGrid's Suppression Management API — not fully explored here).
open_questions: Should the MCP server also integrate SendGrid's Suppression Management API to programmatically clear/check suppressed addresses?
How should cross-channel fallback logic (e.g., email bounced -> try SMS) be orchestrated — in the agent's own logic or a dedicated MCP tool?

tasks.mcp_design_recommendation: Expose a single unified 'get_notification_status(message_id)' tool backed by a small internal datastore that ingests both Twilio status callbacks and SendGrid Event Webhook payloads (verifying signatures on ingestion, not as an MCP tool call) and normalizes them to a common status enum (queued/sent/delivered/failed/bounced/opted_out). The MCP server should expose only read access to this status store to the agent, plus a narrowly-scoped 'suppress_customer(channel, contact)' tool for honoring opt-outs — it should never expose raw webhook-ingestion or provider account-management endpoints directly as agent-callable tools, since those are infrastructure concerns, not agent actions.

cross_task_notes: All communication-channel APIs (SendGrid, Postmark, Twilio SMS/WhatsApp, Vonage) share the pattern: authenticate with a static API key/token, POST a JSON payload describing recipient + template/content, and optionally receive asynchronous webhook callbacks for delivery status. This suggests a clean MCP layering: (1) one or more 'get_order_status' tools per backend (Shopify/WooCommerce) that the agent calls to decide what update to send, (2) one 'send_notification' tool per channel (email/SMS/WhatsApp) that accepts a normalized {recipient, template, variables} shape, and (3) a shared, channel-agnostic 'get_delivery_status' tool backed by a webhook-fed datastore. Because every outbound-messaging API in this space requires either OAuth app approval (Shopify), carrier/BSP registration (Twilio/Vonage SMS, WhatsApp templates), or sender/domain verification (SendGrid/Postmark), the report should flag to the developer that a nontrivial account-setup/compliance phase precedes any code — this is true across every task, not just one. No task in this workflow legitimately needs order-mutating endpoints (create/cancel/refund) — the MCP server should be strictly read-plus-notify to minimize blast radius, since a compromised or misconfigured agent should never be able to alter orders or send unlimited/unthrottled messages. Rate limiting and per-customer message-frequency caps (to avoid spamming, protecting sender/WhatsApp quality reputation) should be enforced in the MCP tool layer itself, not left to the agent's judgment.
